title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第2章
content_zh:
第2章 第一场硬仗

    闹钟响的时候，我正在做梦。

    梦里我还是顾家的女儿，坐在别墅二楼的飘窗上看书，阳光透过白纱窗帘洒在书页上，厨房里飘来李婶炖汤的香味。然后有人敲门，我跑去开门，门外站着顾西辞，他手里拿着一份文件，表情冷得像冰。

    “你不是顾家的女儿。”他说。

    我猛地睁开眼。

    天花板是陌生的。墙角有一块水渍，形状像一张扭曲的脸。楼下传来早点摊的喧哗声，油条的香味混着汽车尾气，从窗缝里挤进来。

    三十七平米的出租屋。

    不是顾家别墅。

    我盯着那块水渍看了几秒，然后爬起来洗漱。热水器坏了一半，水温忽冷忽热，洗到一半彻底凉了。我顶着满头的泡沫等了两分钟，认命了，用冷水冲干净。

    镜子里的人脸色不太好。黑眼圈很重，昨晚翻来覆去到凌晨三点才睡着。眼睛有点肿，好在没哭过——这是底线，我给自己定的。可以失眠，可以焦虑，但不能哭。

    我换上唯一一套拿得出手的职业装——阿玛尼的黑色西装裙，去年顾西辞送的生日礼物。当时他说我穿这个颜色太老气，现在我觉得正好。老气等于稳重，稳重等于靠谱，靠谱等于别人不敢轻易欺负你。

    八点半出门，八点五十到顾氏大厦楼下。

    前台换了人。以前那个叫小周的姑娘不见了，取而代之的是一个我没见过的年轻女孩。她看见我走进来，先是职业微笑，然后目光在我身上快速扫描了一遍——这是受过训练的判断，评估来人的身价和权限。

    “您好，请问有预约吗？”

    “我和顾总有约。”

    “顾总哪个部门的？我帮您查一下。”

    “顾西辞。”

    她的笑容僵了半秒。不是害怕，是那种“你就是那个”的表情。热搜的威力果然大，一夜之间，全城都知道我是谁了。

    “您稍等。”

    她拨了内线，低声说了两句，然后抬头看我，表情恢复了职业化的平静。

    “顾总在二十七楼等您。电梯右手边，直达。”

    我走进电梯，按下二十七。

    镜面电梯里只有我一个人。我对着镜子整理了一下衣领，把嘴角往上提了提。不是笑，是练习笑。昨晚我在备忘录里写了一条——表情管理：面对顾西辞时，保持专业但不过分热情，三分礼貌两分疏离，不能让他觉得我在讨好，也不能让他觉得我在挑衅。

    电梯门开了。

    二十七楼是总裁办公区。我以前来过很多次，那时候前台会笑着叫我“温小姐”，茶水间的阿姨会给我泡桂圆红枣茶。现在茶水间还在，阿姨也还在，但她看见我的时候，目光躲闪了一下，转身去擦桌子了。

    没关系。

    我来这里不是为了叙旧的。

    顾西辞的办公室门虚掩着。我敲了三下。

    “进。”

    他坐在办公桌后面，面前摊着一堆文件，衬衫袖子卷到手肘，领带松松垮垮地挂着。他看我的眼神和昨晚在宴会厅一模一样——公事公办，不带温度。

    “坐。”

    我坐在他对面的椅子上。椅子有点矮，他居高临下地看着我，这个角度是故意设计的，每一个来这间办公室的人都会感受到压迫感。

    “合同你有存档吗？”

    “有。”

    “拿出来。”

    我打开手机，调出加密相册里的合同照片。他把一份打印版推到我面前，上面用红色马克笔圈了几个条款。

    “第三条第二款，‘乙方需配合甲方出席一切必要的商业社交活动’。看到‘必要’两个字了吗？”

    “看到了。”

    “什么是‘必要’，由我来定义。”

    他把另一份文件推过来，是一张日程表，密密麻麻排了一个月。

    “本周五，林氏地产的慈善晚宴。下周三，万盛集团董事会后的答谢酒会。下下周末，青城高尔夫俱乐部的年度邀请赛——”

    他一条一条念下去，语气平淡得像在播天气预报。

    我拿起那张日程表，扫了一眼。

    “高尔夫球我不擅长。”

    “那就学。”

    “一个月学不会。”

    “那是你的问题。”

    我把日程表放下，抬眼看他。

    “顾先生，合同上写的是‘社交应酬按场次另算’，但没有写明具体金额。我的报价是单场三万，超出三小时的部分按加班费另计。”

    他挑了挑眉。

    “你觉得你值这个价？”

    “昨晚你在合同上签了字，说明你觉得我值。”

    沉默。他看着我，我看着他。办公桌上的电子钟跳了一个数字，从九点零五跳到九点零六。

    然后他笑了。

    不是昨晚那种猎人看猎物的笑，是一个商人被对手出了个好价钱时，才会露出的那种带着点欣赏的笑。

    “单场两万。超过三小时的部分按小时计费，时薪两千。”

    “成交。”

    “你连还价都不还？”

    “再还你就该生气了。我现在不想让你生气。”

    他靠在椅背上，双手交叉放在腹部，看我的眼神多了点玩味。

    “温暖，你这么冷静，让我有点不习惯。以前的你不是这样的。”

    “以前的温暖是顾家的女儿，可以任性，可以撒娇，可以一不高兴就摔东西。现在的温暖是顾先生的合约方，任性撒娇摔东西全都不在服务范围内。”

    他的嘴角动了动，像是想说什么，但最终只是把日程表推回给我。

    “周五下午四点，司机会去接你。礼服准备好了，别迟到。”

    “不会。”

    我站起来准备走。走到门口的时候，他叫住我。

    “温暖。”

    “嗯？”

    “昨晚的事——”他顿了顿，“你做得不错。”

    我回头看他。他的表情被逆光遮了一半，看不清楚，但语气里有种说不清道不明的东西。不是夸奖，不是嘲讽，是介于两者之间的、某种不太确定的评价。

    “谢谢顾总。”

    我推门出去，在电梯里才松开握紧的拳头。手心全是汗。

    周五来得很快。

    这中间的三天，我做了三件事。第一件，把林氏地产所有高管的资料查了个遍。林子明，林氏地产的掌门人，五十八岁，白手起家，喜欢抽雪茄、打桥牌、收藏古董表。他太太叫苏婉清，比他小十二岁，婚前是个小有名气的钢琴家，现在主要做慈善，最喜欢的项目是听障儿童康复计划。

    第二件，我去了一趟商城，买了一条不是阿玛尼的裙子。两千块，花了我现在三分之一的积蓄。不是买不起更贵的，是不想再穿顾西辞送的衣服。那条阿玛尼西装裙够用了，但林氏晚宴需要一条正式的礼服裙，这件事我得自己解决。

    第三件，我在知乎上搜了一晚上“桥牌入门”。看到凌晨两点，记住了一个关键信息——桥牌的核心不是牌技，是搭档之间的默契。好的搭档不用说话，一个眼神就知道对方手里的牌。

    周五下午四点，黑色的奔驰准时停在公寓楼下。

    司机不是老陈，换了一个我不认识的年轻人。他看见我从楼道里走出来，愣了一下，然后赶紧帮我拉开车门。

    “温小姐，顾总让我送您去做造型。”

    “不去顾家常去的那家。”

    “啊？”

    “换一家。我认识一个工作室，地址我发给你。”

    他犹豫了一下，但显然接到的指令是“听她的”。我把地址发给他，他看了一眼导航，发动了车子。

    工作室的老板娘叫阿沐，以前是时装周的造型师，后来自己出来单干。我大学时认识她的，那时候她刚开始创业，没什么客户，我找她做过几次造型，她很用心。现在她的工作室已经小有名气，但我和她的交情还在。

    阿沐看见我进来，夸张地吹了声口哨。

    “哎哟，大名人来了。”

    “少来。”

    “我真的看了视频，热搜挂了两天你知道吗？网上有人说你是‘当代甄嬛’。”

    “甄嬛最后出家了，不吉利。”

    她笑着推我坐在化妆镜前，把我的头发拆开，仔细端详了一下我的脸。
content_en:
Chapter 2 The first tough battle
I was dreaming when the alarm clock rang.
In the dream, I was still the daughter of the Gu family, sitting in the bay window on the second floor of the villa reading a book. The sunlight shined on the pages of the book through the white gauze curtains, and the smell of Aunt Li's soup wafted from the kitchen. Then there was a knock on the door, and I ran to open the door. There was Gu Xici standing outside the door. He was holding a document in his hand, and his expression was as cold as ice.
"You are not the daughter of the Gu family," he said.
My eyes shot open.
The ceiling is unfamiliar. There is a water stain in the corner of the wall, shaped like a distorted face. The noise of the breakfast stall came from downstairs, and the smell of fried dough sticks mixed with car exhaust squeezed in through the cracks in the window.
Thirty-seven square meters of rental house.
It's not the Gu family villa.
I stared at the water stain for a few seconds, then got up and washed up. The water heater was half broken, and the water temperature fluctuated between hot and cold. Halfway through the wash, it was completely cold. I waited for two minutes with my head full of foam, then resigned myself to my fate and rinsed it off with cold water.
The person in the mirror doesn't look good. The dark circles under my eyes were so severe that I tossed and turned until three in the morning last night before falling asleep. My eyes were a little swollen, but fortunately I didn’t cry - this is the bottom line I set for myself. You can have insomnia and be anxious, but you can’t cry.
I put on the only professional outfit I could afford—Armani's black suit skirt, which was Gu Xici's birthday gift last year. At the time, he said I was too old-fashioned for wearing this color, but now I think it’s just right. Being old-fashioned means being steady, being steady means being reliable, and being reliable means that others will not dare to bully you easily.
Go out at 8:30 and arrive downstairs at Gu's Building at 8:50.
There was a new person at the front desk. The girl named Xiao Zhou disappeared and was replaced by a young girl I had never seen before. When she saw me walking in, she first smiled professionally, and then quickly scanned me with her eyes - this was a trained judgment, assessing the person's worth and authority.
"Hello, do you have an appointment?"
"I have an appointment with Mr. Gu."
"Which department does Mr. Gu belong to? Let me check for you."
"Gu Xici."
Her smile froze for half a second. Not scared, just that "you're the one" look. The power of hot searches is indeed great. Overnight, the whole city knew who I was.
"Just a moment."
She dialed the internal number, whispered a few words, then looked up at me, her expression returning to a professional calm.
"Mr. Gu is waiting for you on the 27th floor. Directly to the right of the elevator."
I walked into the elevator and pressed twenty-seven.
I was the only one in the mirrored elevator. I straightened my collar in front of the mirror and raised the corners of my mouth. Not laughing, practicing laughing. I wrote an item in my memo last night - expression management: when facing Gu Xici, stay professional but not overly enthusiastic, be polite and distant, and don't make him feel like I'm trying to please, or make him feel like I'm provoking.
The elevator door opens.
The twenty-seventh floor is the president's office area. I have been here many times before. At that time, the front desk would call me "Miss Wen" with a smile, and the aunt in the pantry would make me longan and red date tea. The tea room is still there, and so is my aunt, but when she saw me, her eyes averted for a moment, and she turned around to clean the table.
It doesn't matter.
I'm not here to reminisce.
Gu Xici's office door was ajar. I knocked three times.
"Enter."
He sat behind his desk with a pile of papers spread out in front of him, his shirt sleeves rolled up to his elbows and his tie hanging loosely. The way he looked at me was exactly the same as in the banquet hall last night - businesslike, without warmth.
"sit."
I sat in the chair opposite him. The chair was a bit low, and he looked at me condescendingly. This angle was deliberately designed so that everyone who comes to this office will feel a sense of oppression.
"Do you have the contract on file?"
"have."
"Take it out."
I turned on my phone and pulled up the contract photos in the encrypted photo album. He pushed a printed copy in front of me, with several terms circled in red marker.
"Article 3, Paragraph 2, 'Party B shall cooperate with Party A in attending all necessary business and social activities.' Do you see the word 'necessary'?"
"I saw it."
“What is ‘necessary’ is up to me to define.”
He pushed over another document, which was a schedule that was tightly packed for a month.
"This Friday, Lin's Real Estate's charity dinner. Next Wednesday, the thank you reception after the Wansheng Group's board of directors. Next weekend, Qingcheng Golf Club's annual invitational tournament——"
He read them one by one, his tone as calm as if he was broadcasting a weather forecast.
I picked up the schedule and glanced at it.
"I'm not good at golf."
"Then learn."
"You can't learn it in a month."
"That's your problem."
I put down my schedule and looked up at him.
"Mr. Gu, the contract states that 'social entertainment will be calculated based on the number of sessions', but the specific amount is not stated. My quotation is 30,000 per session, and the portion exceeding three hours will be charged as overtime."
He raised an eyebrow.
"Do you think you're worth the price?"
"You signed the contract last night, which shows that you think I am worth it."
silence. He looked at me and I looked at him. The electronic clock on the desk jumped a number, jumping from nine:05 to nine:06.
Then he laughed.
It's not the kind of smile that a hunter would have when looking at his prey last night, but the kind of appreciative smile that a businessman would show when his opponent offers him a good price.
"Twenty thousand for a single game. The part exceeding three hours will be charged by the hour, and the hourly wage will be two thousand."
"make a deal."
"You don't even pay back the counter-offer?"
"You should be angry if I pay you back. I don't want to make you angry now."
He leaned back in the chair, crossed his hands on his abdomen, and looked at me with a more playful look.
"Nuan Nuan, I'm not used to you being so calm. You were not like this before."
"In the past, Wen Nuan was the daughter of the Gu family. She could be willful, coquettish, and throw things when she was unhappy. Now Wen Nuan is Mr. Gu's contractor. She can be willful, coquettish, and throw things. She is not within the scope of service."
The corners of his mouth moved, as if he wanted to say something, but in the end he just pushed the schedule back to me.
"The driver will pick you up at four o'clock on Friday afternoon. The dress is ready, don't be late."
"Won't."
I stood up to leave. When I reached the door, he stopped me.
"warmth."
"Um?"
"What happened last night -" he paused, "you did a good job."
I looked back at him. His expression was half obscured by the backlight and could not be seen clearly, but there was something inexplicable in his tone. It's not a compliment, it's not a ridicule, it's some kind of uncertain evaluation in between.
"Thank you, Mr. Gu."
I opened the door and went out, and only loosened my clenched fists in the elevator. My palms were sweaty.
Friday comes quickly.
During these three days, I did three things. The first thing is to check the information of all the executives of Lin Real Estate. Lin Ziming, the head of Lin's Real Estate, is fifty-eight years old and started from scratch. He likes smoking cigars, playing bridge, and collecting antique watches. His wife's name is Su Wanqing, who is twelve years younger than him. She was a well-known pianist before marriage. Now she mainly does charity. Her favorite project is the rehabilitation project for hearing-impaired children.
For the second piece, I went to the mall and bought a dress that was not Armani. Two thousand yuan, which cost one-third of my current savings. It wasn't that he couldn't afford more expensive ones, it was just that he didn't want to wear the clothes given by Gu Xici anymore. The Armani suit skirt was adequate, but Lin's dinner required a formal dress, and I had to take care of that myself.
The third thing is that I searched for "Introduction to Bridge" on Zhihu all night. When I saw two o'clock in the morning, I remembered a key message - the core of bridge is not the skill, but the tacit understanding between partners. A good partner doesn't need to speak, he can tell the cards in the opponent's hand just by looking at him.
At four o'clock on Friday afternoon, the black Mercedes-Benz parked under the apartment building on time.
The driver was not Lao Chen, but a young man I didn't recognize. When he saw me walking out of the corridor, he was stunned for a moment, and then quickly opened the car door for me.
"Ms. Wen, Mr. Gu asked me to send you to have your hair styled."
"Don't go to the place where Gu's family usually goes."
"ah?"
"Change one. I know a studio and I'll send you the address."
He hesitated, but was clearly instructed to "listen to her." I sent him the address, he looked at the navigation and started the car.
The proprietress of the studio is called Amu. She used to be a stylist at fashion week, but later she went out on her own. I met her when I was in college. At that time, she just started her business and had few clients. I asked her to do some styling work several times, and she was very attentive. Now her studio has become somewhat famous, but my friendship with her is still there.
Amu saw me coming in and whistled exaggeratedly.
"Ouch, the big name is here."
"Come less."
"I actually watched the video, and it was on the hot search list for two days, you know? Some people on the Internet said that you are a 'contemporary Zhen Huan'."
"Zhen Huan finally became a monk, which is unlucky."
She smiled and pushed me to sit in front of the makeup mirror, untied my hair, and looked at my face carefully.
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 2
